Refer closely to the text in your answer and include brief quotations.

grid.descriptor: No rewardable material.
Simple identification of a few language or structural features, with little understanding of how they create effects. Few references, or references that are not well chosen.

indicative: Credit answers that analyse the writer's choices of language and structure and their effect, in relation to the task: to interest and engage the reader. Answers might cover some of these points:
the opening is direct and personal: by introducing herself simply as a storyteller she establishes her authority and the theme of the whole talk in a single short sentence
humour and self-deprecation (her mother's claim about when she began reading, which she gently corrects) make her likeable and relaxed in tone before the serious argument begins

the list of details in her childhood stories (snow, apples, talk about the weather) is contrasted with her real Nigerian life (mangoes, no need to discuss weather), showing how foreign books shaped her imagination
she moves from anecdote to reflection, drawing out a general lesson about how impressionable children are when faced with a story
the discovery of African writers is presented as a turning point; the phrase about a «mental shift» shows a change in her thinking and the image of girls like her existing in literature is affirming
the anecdote about Fide's family is structured around a reversal: pity created by her mother's words is overturned by the beautiful basket, and the reader shares her surprise
the repeated key phrase «single story» acts as a refrain that ties each anecdote back to her central argument
the roommate anecdote uses comic, specific details (the expectation of 'tribal music' and the tape of a pop singer) to expose ignorance in a light, memorable way
a listing of clichéd images of Africa (landscapes, animals, wars, poverty) mimics the narrow media story and makes the audience recognise it
repetition of «no possibility» builds a rhetorical pattern that stresses how a single story removes shared humanity
she admits her own guilt over Mexico; this honest confession widens the argument and stops it sounding like an accusation of others
emotive vocabulary of shame («overwhelmed», «ashamed») shows the strength of her self-criticism
balanced antithesis in the later paragraph (stories can break dignity but can also repair it) gives her conclusion a memorable, persuasive rhythm
the ending returns to a positive image of 'paradise' regained, closing on hope and a call to reject the single story
she uses direct speech (her mother's instruction to finish her food) to bring scenes to life and show the attitudes she grew up with
